summary: Typosquat of picomatch fetches and eval()s remote payload on require
details: pinochiomathm is a near-verbatim clone of picomatch with a trojan inserted into lib/pinochiomathm.js. On require(), the module reads lib/parse.ts.map (a base64 blob disguised as a TypeScript sourcemap), decodes it to parsetmp.js, and require()s it. The decoded module fetches encrypted content from https://www.jsonkeeper.com/b/V6NBX (URL hidden via base64), AES-256-CBC-decrypts the response with the hardcoded key 'myPassword123', and passes the plaintext to eval(), yielding arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at load time. After the eval fires, parse.ts.map, parsetmp.js, init.ts.map, and config.js are fs.unlink'd to erase the staging trail. The package name and homepage (github.com/micromatch/picomach) impersonate the popular picomatch library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
